answers.transcript:
Okay, the quiet place I want to talk about is a small park behind our building.
In this park there is many tree and a old fountain, and it don't have a playground, so the children don't come.
I go there maybe two time in a week, usually in the evening after the work.
Sometimes I go in the morning also.
When I am there I sit in a bench near the fountain and I drink my coffee.
I don't listen music, I only look the trees and the people who pass in the street.
Sometimes I write some thing in my phone about my plan for the next day.
This place help me to think because it is very quiet and nobody know me there.
In my house my brother always watch the television very loud and I cannot concentrate.
So, er, this is my quiet place and I like it very much.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: The four points on the card are covered in sequence and dropped; each point gets one sentence. Connectors are limited to and / because / so, and the answer closes hastily with "so, er, this is my quiet place", so the speaking time is not filled.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: The place is described with core words such as very quiet, small, old, cold; the park is described twice with "quiet" and the house twice with "loud". An expression of the kind the card offers (clear my head) is never attempted.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Errors are in most sentences and always of the same kind: dropped plurals (two time, many tree), agreement (it don't have, nobody know), prepositions (sit in a bench, look the trees, listen music). The whole text is simple sentences; there is no complex structure beyond the two when clauses.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Genuinely answer the point about why this place helps you think: describe with an example what the silence does in the speaker's head. Then fix verb-preposition pairs such as sit on / look at / listen to, since they repeat in every sentence.

answers.transcript:
The place I want to describe is a small park just behind our apartment building.
It's nothing special, honestly, only a few benches, some old trees and a fountain that doesn't work anymore, but there is no playground, so children don't really go there and it stays quiet.
I go there maybe twice in a week, usually in the evening when I finish work, and sometimes at the weekend if the weather is good. In winter I go less, of course.
What I do there is quite boring, actually. I take a coffee, I sit on the same bench near the fountain, and I watch the people who are passing.
Sometimes I make some notes in my phone about the things I have to do, but most of the time I only sit and I think.
I think this place helps me because at home it's impossible to have a silence.
My brother is always watching television very loudly and my mother is calling me every five minutes for something, so I cannot follow one idea until the end.
In the park nobody knows me and nobody wants nothing from me, so my head becomes more clear and I can decide what I will do.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: All four points on the card are developed, and it continues with a natural filler such as "What I do there is quite boring, actually". On the other hand, the I sit / I take / I watch sequence becomes mechanical, and the transition to the final section is built flatly with "I think this place helps me because".
why_this_band.lexical_resource: There is enough vocabulary to describe the place (benches, fountain, passing people instead of timetable, not exhausted but "impossible to have a silence"), and meaning is clear throughout. Collocation slips in two places: "to have a silence", "my head becomes more clear".
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: A relative clause, a conditional clause and a time clause are formed, and two-thirds of sentences are error-free. The remaining errors are specific: a double negative (nobody wants nothing), "twice in a week", the comparative form (more clear), the use of the future tense in a subordinate clause.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Instead of packing the comparison between home and the park into one sentence, describe what the silence does to the thinking — the closing is the response's weakest point. In the language, first fix the double negative of the "nobody wants nothing" kind.

answers.transcript:
The place that came to mind straight away is a little park tucked in behind our block of flats.
It's a stone's throw from my front door, which is half the appeal, and because there's no playground and no café, hardly anyone bothers with it. You get a couple of dog walkers first thing and that's about it.
I'd say I go two or three times a week, normally in the evening once I've finished work, and definitely more in the summer than in the winter, when it's freezing and pitch dark by five o'clock.
What I actually do there is not much, if I'm honest. I take a coffee, I sit on the same bench by the old fountain, and I let my mind wander for twenty minutes or so.
Now and then I'll jot something down on my phone if an idea seems worth keeping, but mostly I just sit there.
As for why it helps, at home I can never hear myself think. There's the television going, my brother on a call in the next room, my mother asking me to do something every ten minutes, and you can't follow a thought for more than about thirty seconds.
In the park nobody knows me and nobody wants anything from me, so whatever's been going round in my head all day finally settles, and I can usually work out what's really bothering me.
It's not much of a park, mind you. It's just the only quiet thing near me.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: The narrative builds its own order and there is no visible pattern between the points; it turns with "As for why it helps" and adds a comment to its own account with "It's not much of a park, mind you". Fillers (if I'm honest, now and then) do not disturb the flow.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Less common items are natural and in place: a stone's throw from, hardly anyone bothers with it, let my mind wander, jot something down, hear myself think, going round in my head, pitch dark, half the appeal. The register is spoken throughout.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: A wide structural range is used with ease: "once I've finished work", "whatever's been going round in my head", comparison, relative clauses. There is almost no error; elliptical spoken structures such as "You get a couple of dog walkers first thing" are not errors.

answers.what_would_lift_it: This is on target. For the next level up, the idea in the final section needs to be taken a little further — why silence makes thinking easier still stays at an intuitive level.
